A bitterly disappointing experience
Oct 2026 • Friends
The food was good, though not exceptional, but we were very disappointed by the almost non-existent service. It was our final night with friends in Hanoi and we had wanted a special night, so treated ourselves to what we thought would be a ‘fine dining’ experience. We waited a long time after finishing our starters and the staff still hadn’t cleared the dishes before bringing the first of the mains. In fact they didn’t even bother to clear an adjacent table until long after the occupants had left. We were told that two of our choices were sold out (this was 7pm), so imagine our surprise/dismay when guests at a nearby table (who arrived and ordered their meals 30 minutes after us) were served one of the ‘sold out’ dishes. We were advised that two of our mains would take about 30 mins to cook so when one of the other two mains was brought out with still 20 mins to wait, we asked that it be held back until all the mains were ready at the same time. Five minutes later a side dish arrived and we asked for this to be taken back as well. Both dishes were brought back 20 mins later when the others were ready, but were served lukewarm. They had made no effort to reheat it. This is totally unacceptable service for a supposedly fine dining restaurant. My husband asked for another shot of gin to go with the tonic he had left, but they refused to serve gin only. The staff didn’t clear our plates after the main course either. When the bill arrived we asked for the service charge to be taken off. The wait staff looked bewildered and asked why, so we listed the reasons. At no point did she apologise or offer any compensation. We couldn’t wait to leave as the whole experience left us saddened and bitterly disappointed.

A complete letdown at Cao Go
Nov 2025 • Couples
I normally don’t write reviews, but my recent dinner at Cau Go in Hanoi was disappointing enough that I feel the need to share my experience. My wife and I went there based on recommendations from the internet and from our hotel, hoping to enjoy traditional Vietnamese cuisine. Unfortunately, the evening turned out to be quite unpleasant.

To begin with, when we asked for the restroom, we were told it was four floors below in a different restaurant. The facilities were in poor condition, and there was nothing to dry my hands with. When I asked for help, they handed me a single tissue, which felt far from hygienic.

The atmosphere wasn’t any better: the place was very noisy, the décor felt cheap, and the food itself was underwhelming. The beef we ordered was rubbery, the black chicken completely lacked seasoning, and the wine glasses were so small that they held barely two sips. As if that wasn’t enough, a rat ran underneath our table from one side to the other just as we were finishing our meal.

When it came time to pay, our server, Kitty, became unusually pushy about us leaving a positive review on Google. After I told her I would do it later, she went to my wife and insisted again—so persistently that we had to pretend we didn’t have internet access just to end the conversation.

I’m seriously surprised that this place is recommended as “high-end Vietnamese cuisine.” It was honestly the worst restaurant experience I’ve ever had, and I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.

THE QUYNH VAN SHOW!
Apr 2024 • Friends
First things first, I need to shout out our waitress Quynh Van. She was an absolute superstar when helping us with our hotpot. I never seen NOBODY work a hotpot like QV.

I had a vague idea of my way around a hot pot, but QV took us through it step by step, explaining why she is waiting a little extra time to put the egg noodles in, how long the veggies needed to cook for, and even coming and portioning out our servings when the time was right.

It was oddly reminiscent of LeBrons performance in game 5 of the 2007 Eastern Conference finals against the Detroit Pistons, just completely taking over down the stretch. Legacy defining stuff.

Okay – now that that’s out of the way, Cau Go was one of the more expensive meals we had in Vietnam, with entrees being $10-$18 usd. However, after 10 consecutive days of street food with no AC in the blazing heat, to be in a pristine restaurant with a beautiful lake view, quality AC, sensational service, and phenomenal Vietnamese food, it was more than worth it.

We opted to get the chicken salad, spring rolls, stir fried beef, and our beloved hotpot. My buddy wanted to get a frog dish, but for lunch we had witnessed a snake be brutally murdered right in front of our eyes that we then proceeded to eat and drink its blood, so my stomach needed some familiarity. Stir fried beef it was.

Everything was delicious, and I can’t recommend this place enough. We ended up going to Anan in Saigon the next night which has a Michelin star, but I much preferred Cau Go.

After our meal, QV even asked us if we wanted to take a picture of my buddy and I on the rooftop. As is traditional on a boys trip, we had taken next to no pictures together our entire time, so I really appreciate QV for that. She has eyes in the back of her head. She sees everything.

THANK YOU CAU GO! QV NEEDS A RAISE!
